findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor on a datetime and raises TypeError
findings.body: The audit log endpoint uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `getattr(item, self.key)` returns a `datetime`. `get_item_key` then calls `math.floor()` or `math.ceil()` on it, which raises `TypeError`. `build_cursor` calls this key function on every non-empty result set. As a result, any request with `optimized_pagination=true` that returns at least one row fails with a 500. The method copies `Paginator`'s integer logic instead of `DateTimePaginator`'s timestamp conversion.

findings.title: value_from_cursor returns a raw integer for a datetime column
findings.body: `value_from_cursor` returns `cursor.value` unchanged, which is an integer of milliseconds. `build_queryset` then emits `WHERE sentry_auditlogentry.datetime <= %s` with that integer as the parameter. Comparing a timestamp column to an integer either errors in Postgres or filters incorrectly. Any request that sends a cursor with a value breaks. It should convert the value back to a datetime the way `DateTimePaginator` does.

findings.title: Negative QuerySet slicing raises instead of 'efficiently paginating'
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices with `queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `start_offset` is negative. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing; they raise `ValueError` ("Negative indexing is not supported."). A user-supplied cursor such as `0:-5:0` therefore produces a 500 error. The comments claiming 'the Django ORM properly handles negative slicing' and that this 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' are false and misleading. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError`, as `OffsetPaginator` does.

findings.title: BasePaginator change silently clamps or still crashes on negative offsets, with a misleading comment
findings.body: This shared code path is used by `DateTimePaginator`, `Paginator` and others. With the change, a negative offset on a next cursor is silently clamped to 0, returning the first page instead of an error. A negative offset on a prev cursor is still passed straight to the QuerySet slice, which raises `ValueError` and returns a 500. The comment claims 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions', which is not true. Malformed cursors should be rejected explicitly with `BadPaginationError` rather than half-handled across every paginated endpoint.

findings.title: Advanced-pagination gate uses raw is_superuser and can dereference a None member
findings.body: The gate checks `request.user.is_superuser`, which ignores Sentry's active superuser session check (`is_active_superuser(request)`). A superuser without an active superuser session can therefore enable the 'advanced' path. In addition, when the user is not a superuser, `organization_context.member` can be `None` (for example for staff or non-member access paths permitted by `OrganizationAuditPermission`). In that case `.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError` and the request returns a 500, even for requests that never asked for optimized pagination, because the expression is evaluated unconditionally.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported but nothing changed
findings.body: The added comment says `Cursor` allows negative offsets to enable 'efficient reverse pagination'. No code changed here, and negative offsets taken from user-supplied cursor strings lead to crashes in the QuerySet-based paginators. The comment misdocuments the cursor contract.

findings.title: New paginator and endpoint branch have no tests
findings.body: This PR adds `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, changes `BasePaginator` offset handling, and adds a new branch in the audit log endpoint, with no accompanying tests. A basic endpoint test with `optimized_pagination=true` would have caught that the datetime key handling fails on every non-empty page.
